read_many_files_directories.note: Gemini CLI reads a directory entry as `entry/**`; both matchers run these as `read_many_files` `include` lists from the marker directory.

omp_path_grammar.note: OMP's `read` and `write` name a file through a suffix of `path`: a line selector, archive member, SQLite table or row, executable view, video time or query (OMP v18.16.0 tool prompts `read.md` and `write.md`). `readings` are the parts both matchers read beside the path; `vectors` run as `{tool, args: {path}}` payloads from the marker directory, `{root}` standing for it, with `path_count` 1 and `extraction_state` `extracted` unless given. Pi reads the name it is given, so its row keeps.

shell.note: Shell-tool vectors run by both matchers. `{root}` is the marker directory, `cwd` is relative to it, `command` is shorthand for a `bash` payload, and `fold_case` runs the vector as on a case-insensitive (macOS) host.

windows.note: A Windows session (cwd C:\repo) reads Git Bash/MSYS/Cygwin, rooted, device, administrative-share, trailing dot/space and alternate-data-stream spellings as the file they open; both matchers run `files` as an `edit` path and `shell` as a `bash` call.

windows_posix_controls.note: The Windows readings never apply to a POSIX session: there a trailing dot, a colon or a one-letter top-level directory is part of the name.

windows_scopes.note: F1: a device-prefixed cwd and marker directory share the candidates' spelling.
F1: an absolute device-prefixed pattern is spelled like the candidates.
F2: PowerShell and cmd keep a backslash literal, so a bare or double-quoted `\\` path is a UNC or device path.
F3: a native tool reads `/a/x` from the root of the cwd's drive, Git Bash as `A:\x`; both readings count.
A Windows shell word the matcher cannot place (a drive-relative `C:x`, a device-namespace path naming no drive) proves no miss; PowerShell's `FileSystem::` provider prefix names the path after it.
A POSIX absolute pattern in a Windows marker would match no Windows candidate, so the marker is invalid and fails closed.
A glob or brace segment keeps its trailing dots on Windows: `{.,}.` expands to `..`, so trimming it first would hide the parent step.
